summary.text: 会 is the simplified form of 會, used for meeting, gathering, and an organization. Its visible 人 and 云 shapes come from later cursive writing, not an original “person and cloud” construction.

formation.text: 会 is a derived graphic form of 會. One analysis of 會 reads its early construction as 合 with a vessel-like element, suggesting parts fitted together; Xu Shen’s older account instead analyzes 亼 and an abbreviated 曾. The precise object and original sense remain uncertain.

components.text: 人 is visible in the upper part of 会 because this shape developed through cursive writing. It is not supported as a historical semantic or pictorial component.
云 is visible in the lower part of 会 because this shape developed through cursive writing. It is not supported as a historical semantic or phonetic component.

history.text: The graph 会 arose in cursive writing as a variant of 會, became common in later regular script, and was adopted as the simplified form. Its modern division into 人 and 云 should not be projected back onto the ancient graph.
Early forms of 會 have been analyzed as 合 with a vessel-like element; another historical analysis describes 亼 and an abbreviated 曾. Accounts differ over the central shape and the object it represents.

uncertainties.text: A fragmentary oracle-bone phrase 會我 may mean “meet,” but the reading is tentative. The reported bronze and Warring States examples attest meeting or joining, yet do not show whether a vessel or lid sense came first or establish a path from “fit together” to “meet.”
No phonetic role is established for 云 in 会. Historical pronunciation records concern 會 itself and do not give a sound comparison between 云 and 会.

senses.period: Warring States and later securely reported; earlier oracle-bone use tentative
senses.text: Reported bronze and Warring States examples use 會 for meeting at a place, joining ideas, and meeting in alliance. A fragmentary oracle-bone example may have the sense “meet,” but that reading is tentative.
会 is also a noun meaning a meeting or gathering. In Japanese, え is recorded for a gathering, especially a religious assembly, in an early ninth-century text.
会 also means an organization or association. The development of this sense from “meeting” or “gathering” is not dated here.

senses.period: historical; chronology relative to meeting unresolved
senses.text: Historical dictionary citations attest 會 as a noun meaning “lid” or “cover.” This sense fits some proposed readings of the graph’s vessel-like forms, but does not prove that interpretation or establish which sense came first.

developments.text: The noun “meeting” plausibly relates to the verb “meet,” but the attestations do not document when or how that shift occurred.

limitations.text: The earliest secure dating of “meet” or “assemble” relative to “lid” or “cover” is unresolved. A connection from fitting a lid to joining or meeting remains an interpretation rather than a demonstrated sequence.

overview.text: 会 is the simplified form of 會 and means to meet, gather, or a meeting. Its 人-and-云 appearance reflects later cursive writing, rather than an original “person and cloud” construction.

components.text: This is visible in the later form, but is not supported as an ancient component meaning “person.”
This is visible in the later form, but is not supported as an ancient sound cue for 会.

relationships.text: 人 is visible in the later cursive-derived form, but is not supported as a historical semantic, pictorial, or phonetic component of 会.
云 is visible in the later cursive-derived form, but is not supported as a historical semantic or phonetic component of 会.
会 arose as a cursive-derived graphic form of 會 and was adopted as its simplified form.
